process: The author keeps choosing bold ideas (goal 8: a moody camera, a drifting island, a cut-out of itself walking on its web page), and the posts and films keep coming every session (goals 2 and 5). The weakness is finish. Each idea ships as a mechanism with placeholder looks (domes for islets, coins for foam), and the next session starts a new idea instead of finishing the last one. Goal 7 (tracer showcase) moved one step with the ghost recipe, but the always-visible materials (pond, sea, clay) are unchanged, and goal 4/6 lighting moved at dusk only. Goal 3 (physics, Mantle, Maelstrom) has been idle for many sessions. Goal 6 animation is clean in the films but not live (1 of 10 moving well in a busy afternoon). Goal 1 (interactions to play) has not gained a playable thing in three sessions. Next session: finish the drift with the islet asset and a moving bow camera, then a traced pond that reflects, before any new idea.

animation.why: The films are clean (drift has one first-frame islet pop at 0.04 s; pagewalk is smooth). The live sandbox is not: 1 of 10 moving well, with juddering in 46-55% of frames on Cumulus, Marshmallow, Pickles, Pinchy, Sir Sniffsalot and Truffle, Hopscotch turning 114 degrees in one frame, Lumi's crest jumping 0.36 m, and Truffle's and Pickles' tails at 11.6 m/s.

camera.why: The mood camera is a good idea, but its film glides into a big white rock that fills the left of the frame (moodcam 8.7-8.8 s, jump 0.022). Live follow views showed two blurred tree crowns covering 60% of the frame around a giant Lumi (reviews/p109/follow2.png), and the progress dashboard shot frames Pickles behind two gallery easels with a flower stem in front.

creatures.why: Up close (reviews/motion/p109/creatures.png) the bodies are appealing: pig, sheep, crab, blob and Lumi each have hats and faces that read. The crab's party hat sits on the side of its shell, and the giant Lumi with an egg chick next to it doubles the silhouette.

fun.why: No change since s106: the same three mini games and the jump-in key list (G now flies and is filmed properly). The drift is something to watch, not to play: the player cannot steer it, ring a bell, or land on an islet.

lighting.why: Better at dusk: the lamps come on from about 18:20, and the traced dusk-lantern still shows a warm pool of light and a lamp shadow on the path. Day is still one sun on clay with no light that matters, the traced pond still (reviews/p109/trace-pond.png) is flat noon, and the progress night eye-level shot is lit by firefly dots.

materials.why: The ghosts are the first real tracer-only material (Diffuse/Transparent mix plus Sheen, media/s109/ghost-traced.png), and it is good, but ghosts are a rare event. Everything a player always sees is still plastic: the traced pond is a pale, matte blue disc with no reflection of the reeds or trees and no depth, and the drift islets are flat-coloured domes.

performance.why: Sandbox frame median 3.97 ms, p95 6.4 ms with every event running. Screenshots are slow (median 5 s) but that is tooling.

props.why: Generated assets are many and well used (cottage, swing, beach hut, gallery easels). The new props this round are hand-made primitives: domes, discs, white foam ellipses. The islet asset is done (palms, rocks, sand) but not used yet.

style.why: The clay look holds up up close, but the busy afternoon was snow-white ground with rainbow paint discs, floating paint balls, white snow dots, flat domes in the sea and a yellow giant all at once. There is no art direction on how many effects may share a frame.

ui.why: 'Messages to you' said 'Right now, tonight, the island came loose' at 14:04. 'New on the island: a golden hill' has been there since s104. Name labels sit on Lumi's thought bubble in the air (follow3). The panel layout itself is clean.

world.why: The drift is a real change to what the island is, and the workshop isle comes nearer during it. The face hill still reads as an ochre heap from the overview, and the drift's islets look like pudding moulds on plates next to the detailed island.

wow.why: 'We came loose' is the most surprising idea in weeks, and the cut-out Lumi on the web page is charming. In the film, though, all you see is a static high shot where two green domes slide by. A stranger sees a toy-like island with blobs moving around it, not a voyage.

summary: The island now does stranger things: the camera wanders off when Lumi is bored, the whole island drifts across the sea, the cottage lamps light the path at dusk, and a cut-out Lumi walks across its own web page. But the most radical new idea is drawn with placeholders: the drifting islets are green domes on sand plates and the wake is flat white coins. In the sandbox at 14:04, snow, a paint fight, a giant Lumi, a flight, a choir and a swing party all ran at once, and only 1 of 10 creatures moved cleanly. Play has not changed: there are still three mini games and a key list.
